[L1] {
[L2]   "content": "# @earendil-works/pi-durable\n\n> **Experimental.** The API changes without notice between releases.\n\nA durable agent harness. Conversations, model turns, tool calls, and your own state are committed to storage before anything is shown. If the process dies mid-turn, reopening the storage picks the work up where it stopped.\n\nBuilt on [`@earendil-works/pi-ai`](../ai/README.md) for model access and `@earendil-works/chord` for document state.\n\n## Table of Contents\n\n- [Installation](#installation)\n- [Quick Start](#quick-start)\n- [Concepts](#concepts)\n- [Persist and Resume](#persist-and-resume)\n- [Extensions](#extensions)\n- [Tools](#tools)\n- [Code Mode](#code-mode)\n- [System Prompt](#system-prompt)\n- [Per-Conversation Agent](#per-conversation-agent)\n- [Settings](#settings)\n- [Environment](#environment)\n- [Reload](#reload)\n- [Watching a Conversation](#watching-a-conversation)\n- [Busy Conversations](#busy-conversations)\n- [Reset and Handoff](#reset-and-handoff)\n- [Compaction](#compaction)\n- [Agent Events (Experimental)](#agent-events-experimental)\n- [Hooks](#hooks)\n- [More Conversations and Forks](#more-conversations-and-forks)\n- [Abort and Subagents](#abort-and-subagents)\n- [Child Tasks](#child-tasks)\n- [Task Graph](#task-graph)\n- [Your Own State](#your-own-state)\n- [Usage and Cost](#usage-and-cost)\n- [Storage](#storage)\n- [Errors](#errors)\n- [Examples](#examples)\n- [Design Documents](#design-documents)\n\n## Installation\n\n```bash\nnpm install @earendil-works/pi-durable @earendil-works/pi-ai @earendil-works/chord\n```\n\n## Quick Start\n\n```typescript\nimport { BACKGROUND_CONTEXT } from \"@earendil-works/chord/context\";\nimport { createModels } from \"@earendil-works/pi-ai/models\";\nimport { openaiProvider } from \"@earendil-works/pi-ai/providers/openai\";\nimport { AssistantEntry, createRegistry, Harness, MemoryStorage } from \"@earendil-works/pi-durable\";\n\nconst context = BACKGROUND_CONTEXT;\n\nconst models = createModels();\nmodels.setProvider(openaiProvider()); // reads OPENAI_API_KEY\n\nconst harness = await Harness.open(new MemoryStorage(), { models, registry: createRegistry() }, context);\nconst root = await harness.root(context, { agent: { model: { provider: \"openai\", modelId: \"gpt-6-sol\" } } });\n\nconst submission = await root.submit({ type: \"input\", content: \"What is the capital of France?\" }, context);\nconst settled = await submission.wait(context);\nif (settled.status === \"done\" && settled.type === \"input\") {\n\tconst answer = await root.commit((tx) => tx.entry(AssistantEntry, settled.answer), context);\n\tconsole.log(answer?.model?.[0]);\n}\nawait harness.close(context);\n```\n\nWhat happened:\n\n- `Harness.open()` opens a Session over a storage backend. `MemoryStorage` keeps everything in memory.\n- `root()` returns the root conversation, creating it on first use with the given agent choices. A conversation is a transcript of immutable entries.\n- `submit()` durably admits your input and returns a `Submission`. A built-in generation task calls the model and appends the answer.\n- `wait()` resolves once the input is answered (`done`) or has failed (`unanswered`, with a reason).\n\nEvery async call takes a Chord `Context`, which carries cancellation. `BACKGROUND_CONTEXT` never cancels. Cancelling a wait only cancels that wait, never the work.\n\n## Concepts\n\n- **Harness**: one open storage plus the machinery that runs agents on it. All changes go through one line of atomic commits, and nothing is shown before its commit is stored.\n- **Conversation**: a transcript. `root()` creates the root conversation on first use; you can create more and fork them. A `Conversation` handle holds no state; compare handles by `id`.\n- **Entry**: one immutable transcript record, such as a user message (`pi.user`), a model response (`pi.assistant`), a tool result (`pi.tool-result`), a system prompt change (`pi.system`), a reset (`pi.reset`), or your own kind. The model sees the entries from the newest reset onward.\n- **Commit**: an atomic write. `conversation.commit((tx) => ...)` can append entries, edit documents, and create tasks together; either all of it is stored or none of it.\n- **Document**: typed JSON state stored next to the transcript and changed in commits. Built-in ones hold each conversation's agent choices (`pi.agent`), provider-facing session identity (`pi.provider`), running generation and tools (`pi.live`), queued submissions (`pi.inbox`), and spend (`pi.usage`).\n- **Task**: a durable state machine that saves a checkpoint at every step, so a restarted process continues from the last one. Every task has an owner: its conversation, or another task. The Harness runs answers as built-in tasks: `pi.generation` calls the model and owns the `pi.tool` tasks of its tool calls, waits for them, and hands the run to the next generation.\n- **Submission**: something you hand to a conversation, either user input or an entry to write, which you can wait for.\n- **Turn and run**: a turn is one model response and its tool calls; a run is the turns from an input to its final answer. A conversation is busy while a run is going.\n- **Extension**: a named bundle of tools, system prompt sections, hooks, wrappers, and tasks.\n- **Registry**: the extensions this process installed. It can change while the Harness runs; new work uses the new state.\n- **Agent**: what a conversation runs with: model, thinking level, selected extensions, tools, instructions, and working directory. Stored per conversation as names in `pi.agent`, resolved against the registry at each use.\n\nOne answered input, as entries and tasks:\n\n```text\nsubmit(input) → pi.user\n  pi.generation → pi.system (only if the prompt or tools changed), pi.assistant (tool calls)\n    pi.tool × n → pi.tool-result × n   (owned by the generation, which waits for them)\n  pi.generation → pi.assistant (answer) → submission done\n```\n\n## Persist and Resume\n\nUse SQLite or JSONL storage to keep conversations across restarts:\n\n```typescript\nimport { openNodeSqliteStorage } from \"@earendil-works/pi-durable/storage/sqlite/node\";\n\nconst harness = await Harness.open(await openNodeSqliteStorage(\"./session.sqlite\"), { models, registry }, context);\nconst root = await harness.root(context); // the same root as last time\nharness.resume(); // continue any run the last process left unfinished\n```\n\nWork interrupted by a crash or close stays pending. `resume()` starts the task scheduler; submitting or waiting starts it too. Each conversation has its own persisted UUIDv7 in `pi.provider`, forwarded to pi-ai as `sessionId` for provider prompt-cache and session affinity. It survives reopen, retries, reset, compaction, and model changes; a child or fork receives a fresh identity. A legacy conversation receives and persists one before its first generation or compaction request.\n\nA retried submission with the same `requestId` returns the existing submission instead of submitting twice:\n\n```typescript\nconst submission = await root.submit({ type: \"input\", content: \"Hello\", requestId: \"greeting-1\" }, context);\n// After a restart: the same request ID finds the same submission.\nconst again = await root.submit({ type: \"input\", content: \"Hello\", requestId: \"greeting-1\" }, context);\n// again.id === submission.id\n```\n\n`harness.submission(id)` reacquires a submission by ID, for example to wait for it after a restart.\n\n## Extensions\n\nCode the Harness runs, other than its built-in tasks, comes in named extensions installed in a registry your process owns:\n\n```typescript\nimport { createRegistry, defineExtension, defineTool, hook, section, ToolTask } from \"@earendil-works/pi-durable\";\nimport { CodingTools } from \"@earendil-works/pi-durable/tools\";\n\nconst Coding = defineExtension({\n\tname: \"coding\",\n\tsections: [section(\"preamble\", () => \"You are a concise coding assistant.\", { tag: false })],\n\thooks: [hook(ToolTask, { beforeTool: (call) => (isDangerous(call) ? { block: \"Needs approval\" } : undefined) })],\n});\n\nconst registry = createRegistry();\nregistry.install(CodingTools);\nregistry.install(Coding);\n```\n\nAn extension may bring `tools`, `sections`, `hooks`, `wraps` (decorators of a tool or section by name), and `tasks`. By default every conversation selects every installed extension, in install order. Nothing in the registry is stored; conversations store extension names.\n\n## Tools\n\n`@earendil-works/pi-durable/tools` provides `read`, `write`, `edit`, and `bash`, and the `CodingTools` extension with all four. They touch files and processes only through the call's environment (see [Environment](#environment)).\n\n`read` returns an image file as one image block, which programs calling it get as an `ImageContent`. Limits are the model's `inputLimits.images.resize`, by default 2000x2000 pixels and 4.5 MB of base64. Without an image processor it sends PNG, JPEG, GIF, and WebP files within them (dimensions read from the file's header) as they are, without decoding them, and refuses larger ones and other formats. With one, it decodes every image, turns it upright by its EXIF orientation, converts BMP to PNG, and shrinks it to fit. The Photon-based processor runs on WebAssembly and is only loaded when you import it:\n\n```typescript\nimport { createNodePhotonImages } from \"@earendil-works/pi-durable/images/node\"; // or /images/cloudflare, or createPhotonImages(wasm) from /images\nimport { createCodingTools } from \"@earendil-works/pi-durable/tools\";\n\nregistry.install(createCodingTools({ images: await createNodePhotonImages() }));\n```\n\nA model without image input sees a placeholder instead of the image, and `read` says so in a diagnostic. `/images/node` prepares images in a worker thread, so a large photo (a second or two of work) never blocks the event loop; the worker exits after 30 s without images, freeing Photon's WebAssembly memory (`createNodePhotonImages({ worker: false, idleMs })`). Elsewhere, `createPhotonImages()` and `/images/cloudflare` work on the calling thread, and decoding takes the image's full size in WebAssembly memory, which does not shrink again; leave the processor out on memory-constrained hosts such as Cloudflare Workers unless images stay small.\n\nDefine your own tool with a TypeBox schema. `defineTool()` types `args` from `parameters`, which the Harness validates before `execute()`. `api.output()` streams running output, which becomes the result when `execute()` returns no `output`:\n\n```typescript\nimport { Type } from \"@earendil-works/pi-ai\";\n\nconst count = defineTool({\n\tname: \"count\",\n\tdescription: \"Count from 1 to n\",\n\tparameters: Type.Object({ n: Type.Number() }),\n\texecute: async (args, api) => {\n\t\tfor (let i = 1; i <= args.n; i++) api.output(`${i}\\n`);\n\t\treturn {};\n\t},\n});\nregistry.install(defineExtension({ name: \"count\", tools: [count] }));\n```\n\nEach call runs as its own durable task. Its intent is committed before `execute()` runs. If the process dies mid-call, the tool reruns on reopen only when it is declared `replay: \"safe\"`; otherwise the model gets an `interrupted` error result with the output committed so far. Throwing from `execute()` gives the model an error result. A result can also return `usage`, which is added to the conversation's [usage](#usage-and-cost). It can also return `control: { terminate: true }`: when every result of the round asks for it, the run ends without another model request.\n\nA result has three channels: `output` for the model, `structuredOutput` for programs that call the tool (see [Calling tools from tools](#calling-tools-from-tools)), and `details` for UIs. A tool that declares `structuredOutputSchema` returns a matching `structuredOutput`, which the Harness validates. Programs calling a tool without one get its bounded output: one text item as a string, one image as its `ImageContent`, nothing as `\"\"`, and anything else as the content list, for errors too. `structuredOutput` is always the tool's own value: a schema tool's error result keeps the value it returned, and the text of one without is in a `tool_error` diagnostic, as a thrown error's message is. The transcript stores only `output` and `details`:\n\n```typescript\nconst lines = defineTool({\n\tname: \"lines\",\n\tdescription: \"Count the lines of a file\",\n\tparameters: Type.Object({ path: Type.String() }),\n\tstructuredOutputSchema: Type.Object({ lines: Type.Number() }),\n\texecute: async (args, api, context) => {\n\t\tconst text = await readText(api, args.path, context);\n\t\tconst count = text.split(\"\\n\").length;\n\t\treturn { output: [{ type: \"text\", text: `${count} lines` }], structuredOutput: { lines: count } };\n\t},\n});\n```\n\nA missing, undeclared, or invalid `structuredOutput` turns a nested call's result into an error result with an `invalid_structured_output` diagnostic; for a call the model made, which never sees it, it is dropped and reported through `onReport`. An error result may omit it, and programs then find its text in a `tool_error` diagnostic; error results the Harness writes itself (blocked, invalid, interrupted, aborted) carry none, and their `diagnostics` say what went wrong. An `afterTool` hook that redacts a schema tool's `output` must redact its `structuredOutput` too. The built-in `bash` returns `{ output, truncated, fullOutputPath?, exitCode }`, where `output` is the retained tail the model sees, read with `api.retainedOutput()`, and answers a nonzero exit with an error result that still carries it.\n\nA later extension's tool with the same name replaces an earlier one where both are selected, and `wrapTool()` decorates whichever tool won:\n\n```typescript\nconst Venv = defineExtension({ name: \"venv\", tools: [createBashTool({ commandPrefix: \"source .venv/bin/activate\" })] });\nconst Timing = defineExtension({\n\tname: \"timing\",\n\twraps: [wrapTool(createBashTool(), (bash) => ({ ...bash, execute: (args, api, ctx) => timed(() => bash.execute(args, api, ctx)) }))],\n});\n```\n\n### Calling tools from tools\n\nA tool calls another tool with `api.executeTool()`, as a code mode script or an MCP bridge does. The nested call is its own tool task, owned by the calling one: it is validated, runs the `ToolTask` hooks, keeps its own output limits and replay policy, and returns its result to the caller instead of the transcript:\n\n```typescript\nconst testsPass = defineTool({\n\tname: \"tests_pass\",\n\tdescription: \"Run the test suite and say whether it passed\",\n\tparameters: Type.Object({}),\n\texecute: async (_args, api, context) => {\n\t\tconst run = await api.executeTool(\"bash\", { command: \"npm test\" }, context, { progress: false });\n\t\t// Absent when bash did not finish, for example on a timeout.\n\t\tconst exitCode = (run.structuredOutput as { exitCode: number } | undefined)?.exitCode;\n\t\treturn { output: [{ type: \"text\", text: exitCode === 0 ? \"passed\" : \"failed\" }] };\n\t},\n});\n```\n\n- The caller gets the nested call's `taskId`, `structuredOutput`, `details`, `diagnostics`, `usage`, and `isError`, not the `output` meant for the model. A blocked, invalid, failed, or aborted nested call returns an `isError` result. `executeTool()` itself rejects once `execute()` has returned, when the caller is aborted, or when the Harness closes; cancelling its `context` stops only the wait.\n- Hooks see a nested call's `call.parent`, so a guard can treat calls from scripts differently.\n- While the caller runs, its nested calls show in `docs[\"pi.live\"].nestedTools`, with the arguments they run with and a `summary` (error, duration, usage) once done, and as tool events with `parentToolCallId` and `parentTaskId`. `progress: false` keeps a nested call's running output out of `pi.live`. Before the caller settles, nested calls it left running are aborted, also those an earlier attempt made. The caller's result message does not list its nested calls;... (truncated)

Before the caller settles, nested calls it left running are aborted, also those an earlier attempt made. The caller's result message does not list its nested calls; their task records keep them.\n- Each nested call has a key, its position among the caller's nested calls unless the caller passes `{ key }`. A replay-safe caller that reruns after a crash and calls in the same order, or passes the same keys, gets the nested calls it already made back, finished or still running, instead of starting them again. A nested call the crash interrupted before its result was committed follows its own `replay` policy, so a replay-safe tool with external effects still needs its own idempotency. A caller that is not replay-safe never reruns, so after a restart its unfinished nested calls are abandoned, with everything they own, before they run again.\n- A nested call's `usage` is counted under its own tool; passing it on in the caller's result counts it twice.\n- Nested results are not kept: they live in the caller's task documents (`NestedCallDoc`, one per nested call, keyed by its key, holding `{ taskId, result? }`) only until the caller settles. The nested call's task record keeps only a small receipt. A stored result is exactly what `executeTool()` returns, without the model's `output`, so an image or a `bash` tail is stored once.\n- Nothing bounds how deeply calls nest; a tool with the default `callers` may even call itself. Restrict `callers` where that matters (below).\n\n### Who may call a tool\n\n`callers` on a tool says who may call it: the model, other tools through `executeTool()`, or both, the default. A conversation's `modelTools` narrows which of its tools the model is offered, without taking them away from tools:\n\n```typescript\nconst codemode = defineTool({ name: \"codemode\", callers: [\"model\"], ... }); // scripts cannot start scripts\nconst search = defineTool({ name: \"mcp__github__search\", callers: [\"tools\"], ... }); // never offered to the model\n\n// The model is offered only codemode; its scripts call read, bash, and the MCP tools.\nawait root.configure({ modelTools: [codemode] }, context);\n// The model is offered everything but bash, which scripts may still call.\nawait root.configure({ modelTools: { remove: [bash] } }, context);\n```\n\n`conversation.agent()` resolves both lists: `tools`, offered to the model, and `callable`, which nested calls resolve among. `tools` still decides what is enabled at all; `modelTools` cannot add to it.\n\nA `deferred: true` tool is not offered to the model until it is loaded, though other tools can call it any time. The `tool_search` tool from `@earendil-works/pi-durable/tool-search` (`createToolSearchExtension()`) lets the model search the deferred tools and loads the matches with `control.addTools`, which records them in `modelTools`; loaded tools stay offered on that branch, also after a compaction, and the `codemode` section leaves deferred tools out. Use it for large tool sets, such as an MCP server's.\n\n### Tasks a restart abandons\n\nA task that its creator awaits only in memory, and that the creator never resumes after a restart, can be created with `abandonOnRestart: true`. When a later Harness starts scheduling and finds it still live, it is aborted with `abortReason: \"restart\"`, together with everything it owns, before any of it runs again. Nested calls of tools that are not replay-safe get this automatically, and so do the child tasks such a tool creates with `api.createTask()`. A task abandoned this way whose definition is missing waits until its extension is installed, so its abort handler still cleans up. Its caller, and the conversation, wait with it; `harness.inspect()` shows it as blocked. Aborting it then orphans it, as any abort does.\n\n## Code Mode\n\n`@earendil-works/pi-durable/codemode` adds a `codemode` tool: the model writes JavaScript that calls the conversation's tools as `await tools.<name>(args)`, in a QuickJS sandbox (`@earendil-works/pi-codemode`). Each call is a nested tool call, and only the script's output reaches the model. The script survives a restart: it resumes where it was, without running its finished calls again.\n\n```typescript\nimport { CodemodeSandbox } from \"@earendil-works/pi-codemode\";\nimport { createCodemodeExtension } from \"@earendil-works/pi-durable/codemode\";\n\nregistry.install(createCodemodeExtension({ sandbox: new CodemodeSandbox({ memoryLimitBytes: 256 * 1024 * 1024 }) }));\n```\n\nThe extension also adds a `codemode` prompt section listing the tools scripts can call, as TypeScript declarations within a token budget; scripts find the others with `searchTools()`, `describeTool()`, and `describeNamespace()`. Group tools by name prefix with `namespaces: [{ name, description, prefix }]`, for example an MCP server's `mcp__github__`. The result reads like the coding agent's: a header, the script's output, and on failure the calls already made; text past `max_output_tokens` is cut, with the full text in a temp file. Scripts also get `models.*`: the model catalog, `models.classify()`, and `models.generateImages()`, which run as nested calls of internal tools (`models: false` turns them off). On Cloudflare, pass a `RemoteCodemodeSandbox` instead. Closing the sandbox while a script runs (for example when shutting down) is not an outcome: the script resumes with the next process's sandbox. A failed nested call rejects in the script with its error text, unless the tool declares a schema and returned its own value with the error: `tools.bash` resolves with `{ output, exitCode, ... }` also for a nonzero exit, so scripts check `exitCode`. `store(key, value)` and `load(key)` keep JSON values per conversation; a fork sees them as they were at its entry.\n\nHow it survives a restart: the sandbox runs the script deterministically (a virtual clock, seeded randomness, UTC), and the tool writes each result the script gets to a journal before handing it over. After a restart, the tool runs the script again and hands it the journaled results in the same order, so it makes the same calls with the same arguments; these reattach to their nested calls by key, and then the script continues. A rerun ends the call with an error instead when the script takes another path than before, when the sandbox's fingerprint or the code mode version changed, or when its `timeout_ms` passed meanwhile. A nested call running at the restart follows its own replay policy.\n\n## System Prompt\n\nThe system prompt is built from the selected extensions' sections, rendered in order before each request. Sections and tool changes are stored as positional system entries in the transcript. Only what changed is sent again, which keeps provider prompt caches warm. A section that returns something different every time, such as the current time, defeats that.\n\n## Per-Conversation Agent\n\nEach conversation stores what it runs with in its `pi.agent` document. `configure()` changes it in one commit; unset fields follow the host:\n\n```typescript\nawait root.configure(\n\t{\n\t\tmodel: { provider: \"openai\", modelId: \"gpt-6-sol\" },\n\t\tthinkingLevel: \"high\",\n\t\textensions: { remove: [Coding] }, // edits the host default; an array selects exactly these, in order\n\t\ttools: [readTool, bashTool], // an array enables exactly these; { remove: [...] } drops some\n\t\tmodelTools: [readTool], // of those, offer the model only read; tools may still call bash\n\t\tinstructions: \"Only read; never edit files.\",\n\t\tcwd: \"/work/repo\",\n\t},\n\tcontext,\n);\nawait root.configure({ tools: null }, context); // null clears a field back to the host default\nconst agent = await root.agent(context); // resolved: model, extensions, tools, sections, cwd\n```\n\nExtensions and tools are passed as objects and stored by name, so a stored name outlives its code: after an extension is uninstalled, conversations that select it just stop getting it until it is installed again. `createConversation()`, `fork()`, and `root()` take the same change as `agent`. A task-owned conversation, such as a subagent's, starts as a copy of its owner's conversation's agent. A fork starts with the agent its parent had at the fork entry. The model, prompt, and offered tools of a request are fixed when it is prepared; a change applies from the next request. Tool calls and hooks use the agent as their task phase resolves it, and the environment is built from the current `cwd` at each use, so a `cwd` or extension change can reach calls the model already made.\n\n## Settings\n\nRun policy shared by every conversation is passed as `settings`. Keeps the whole history in memory too, so memory grows with it; use SQLite for long-running agents. |\n| Cloudflare Durable Object | `openDurableObjectSqliteStorage(ctx.storage)` from `@earendil-works/pi-durable/storage/sqlite/cloudflare` | The SQLite storage of one SQLite-backed Durable Object; commits are its storage transactions. |\n\nSQLite storage can namespace its tables and indexes when sharing a database: pass `{ prefix: \"pi_\" }` to\n`SqliteStorage.open(database, options)`, `openNodeSqliteStorage(path, options)`, or\n`openDurableObjectSqliteStorage(ctx.storage, options)`. Storage renders the prefixed names into its SQL, so adapters\nneed no support. A prefix must be a SQLite identifier and cannot begin with `sqlite_`; a host may reserve more, such\nas `_cf_` in Durable Objects. Changing the prefix does not migrate existing data.\n\nMultiple Pi storages opened through the Cloudflare adapter with the same storage object automatically share an\noperation queue. To share the database with host tables, create an adapter and use it for both Pi and all host queries;\ndirect storage calls bypass the queue and may be rolled back with a Pi transaction:\n\n```typescript\nconst database = new DurableObjectSqliteDatabase(ctx.storage);\nconst piStorage = await SqliteStorage.open(database, { prefix: \"pi_\" });\nawait database.exec(\"CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS host_notes (text TEXT)\");\nawait database.run(\"INSERT INTO host_notes (text) VALUES (?)\", text);\n```\n\nOne process owns a storage at a time; there is no cross-process locking. The portable SQLite and JSONL cores (`/storage/sqlite`, `/storage/jsonl`) run without Node APIs, for example on Bun or in Cloudflare Durable Objects, given an asynchronous `SqliteDatabase` facade or a `FileSystem` from `@earendil-works/pi-durable/env`.\n\nSQLite adapters implement promise-based `exec`, `run`, `get`, `all`, `transaction`, and `close`. `run`, `get`, and `all` take SQL text plus positional bindings; adapters may cache prepared statements by SQL text. A transaction callback receives a transaction handle; all work in the transaction must use it, and the handle expires when the callback settles. Adapters must queue unrelated operations and other transactions until the transaction finishes, so calling `database` itself inside the callback never settles:\n\n```typescript\nawait database.transaction(async (transaction) => {\n\tawait transaction.exec(\"CREATE TABLE example (value TEXT)\");\n\tawait transaction.run(\"INSERT INTO example (value) VALUES (?)\", \"stored atomically\");\n});\n```\n\nCustom backends can run the shared conformance suite with any Vitest- or Jest-compatible runner:\n\n```typescript\nimport { registerStorageConformance } from \"@earendil-works/pi-durable/testing\";\nimport { describe, expect, it } from \"vitest\";\n\nregisterStorageConformance({ describe, expect, it }, \"My Storage\", async (use) => {\n\tconst storage = await openMyStorage();\n\ttry {\n\t\tawait use(storage);\n\t} finally {\n\t\tawait closeMyStorage(storage);\n\t}\n});\n```\n\nThe package root loads TypeBox, because the tool task validates arguments with pi-ai's `validateToolArguments()`. That costs about 23 MB of peak RSS unbundled, about 4 MB in a tree-shaken bundle.\n\n## Errors\n\nThree rules decide what an error does:\n\n1. **A storage error ends the Harness.** The call that hit it rejects with the error. Everything after it, and every pending wait, rejects with `SessionFailed` (its `cause` is that error); watches and event streams end with `session_failed`; running tasks get their abort signal; `onReport` gets the error once. The Harness then closes itself. Nothing is retried; a custom storage retries its own transient failures. Reopen to recover: commits are atomic, so the store is consistent, and resubmitting with the same `requestId` finds a submission that was already admitted.\n2. **An invalid request fails only that call:** a storage throws `StorageRequestError` for a bad cursor, an unknown conversation, or history a document does not keep. A read you cancelled fails only itself too.\n3. **Your code fails only its own unit:** a throwing task phase faults that task, a throwing tool gets an error result, a throwing hook is reported and skipped (`beforeTool` blocks the call), and a throwing commit callback rolls back that commit. Listeners that throw, or return a rejected promise, are reported and the others still run. The exception is a host `RegistryReader` whose `snapshot()` throws: the Harness cannot schedule without it, so it fails the Harness like a storage error.\n\n`harness.closed` settles once the Harness has closed, by `close()` or after a storage error, so a host restarts on failure like this:\n\n```typescript\nharness.closed.then((end) => {\n\tif (end.reason === \"failed\") reopen(end.error);\n});\n```\n\nA failure closes the Harness by itself; `closed` settles once that close is done, even if the storage could not close cleanly. Closing waits for running task code to return, so code that ignores its abort signal delays `closed`.\n\n## Examples\n\nRunnable examples live in [`test/examples`](test/examples). So does the call failing: `execute()` throwing, or a crash that interrupts a call that is not replay-safe.\n- The parent is idle only once the child is.\n- A task created with `{ background: true }` is a boundary: work it owns survives the parent's abort and does not keep the parent busy. `root.abort(context, { background: true })` aborts it too.\n\nThe examples show both patterns as product code:\n\n- [`22-subagent-foreground.ts`](test/examples/22-subagent-foreground.ts): the tool above, returning the child's answer. The UI finds the child through the call's `details` and prints the child's events indented under the call.\n- [`23-subagent-background.ts`](test/examples/23-subagent-background.ts): persistent subagents behind one `subagent` tool that spawns, messages (steer or follow-up), waits for, stops, and lists them. Each child is owned by a background anchor task, so the parent's Esc and idle waits never reach it. Each message is delivered by a background reporter task that posts the answer back to the parent as a follow-up input once it arrives; request IDs keep a restart from sending a message or a report twice.\n\n## Child Tasks\n\nA task can own child tasks, created with `ownership: { kind: \"task\", taskId }`, and wait for them by committing a `waiting` state:\n\n```typescript\npay: async (task, runtime, context) => {\n\tawait runtime.commit(async (tx) => {\n\t\tconst payments = [];\n\t\tfor (const card of task.input.cards) {\n\t\t\tpayments.push(await tx.createTask(Payment, { card }, { ownership: { kind: \"task\", taskId: task.id } }));\n\t\t}\n\t\t// Resume in `decide` once every payment is done; the first failure aborts the rest.\n\t\treturn { status: \"waiting\", checkpoint: { phase: \"decide\", payments }, on: payments, policy: \"failFast\" };\n\t}, context);\n},\ndecide: async (task, runtime, context) => {\n\tconst outcomes = await runtime.outcomes(task.state.checkpoint.payments, context);\n\t// ...commit the checkout's own outcome\n},\n```\n\n- **Waiting:** the task runs no code while it waits. With `allSettled` it resumes once every task in `on` is done; with `failFast` the first failed child also aborts the others. `on` may name other tasks too, with `allSettled`.\n- **Finishing:** a task that finishes while work it owns is still running is `completing`: its outcome is decided, but it becomes terminal, and `waitForTask()` returns, only once that work is done. A failed or aborted outcome aborts that work first.\n- **Aborting:** abort runs bottom-up. Aborting a task aborts the work it owns first, and its own abort handler starts only once that work is done, so each task undoes its own effects.\n\n[`24-child-tasks.ts`](test/examples/24-child-tasks.ts) runs a checkout with four payments: a declined card, a cancelled checkout, and a restart while the payments run.\n\n## Task Graph\n\n`harness.taskGraph(context)` shows every live task of the Session as one Chord state, for a task panel or debugging. Each node has its owner edge (`owner` task, or none for a task its conversation owns), its status, whether it is `background` or abort-marked, and the conversations it owns. `harness.watchTaskGraph(context)` delivers the same value as a watch, like a conversation's `watch()`.\n\n```typescript\nconst graph = await harness.taskGraph(context);\ngraph.subscribe((value) => {\n\tfor (const node of Object.values(value.tasks)) {\n\t\tconst status = node.state.status === \"waiting\" ? `waiting on ${node.state.on.join(\", \")}` : node.state.status;\n\t\tconsole.log(`${node.id} ${node.kind} ${status}`, node.owner ?? `conversation ${node.conversationId}`);\n\t}\n});\n```\n\nA task appears with the commit that creates it and leaves with the commit that makes it terminal. Statuses are the committed ones: `pending`, `running`, `waiting` (with `on` and `policy`), and `completing` (with the held outcome's status). After a restart, tasks that were `running` show as `pending` until they run again. Whether a pending task is blocked by a missing definition is not part of the graph; `harness.inspect()` reports that. [1565] assistant (text, 358 chars)
The upstream Pi v1.3.0 documentation exposed a consequential detail: `submission.wait()` does not by itself publish the assistant answer into the durable transcript. The host must commit it. I’m adding that as an atomic, restart-safe completion step so repeated polling cannot create duplicate answer entries, then I’ll run the full checks and build the ZIP.

#!/usr/bin/env python3

import os

from dottie_hill import __file__ as package_file, __version__

    core.memories('aegis-dugan', 'private:dottie-hill')
except AccessDenied:
    pass
else:
    raise AssertionError('private memory was readable across identities')
mission = core.create_mission('operator','dottie-hill','inspect own memory','installed-wheel-read',
    context_scopes=['private:dottie-hill'],execution_mode='codemode')

    {'scope':'private:dottie-hill','limit':1})

reopened.close()
print('PASS: wheel import/version, six identities, private scope denial, signed Code Mode read and ledger restart')
'''


def main() -> int:
    if not WHEEL.is_file():
        print(f'FAIL: wheel not built: {WHEEL}', file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    with TemporaryDirectory(prefix='gmri-wheel-smoke-') as tmp:
        target = Path(tmp) / 'target'
        env = {**os.environ, 'PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE': '1'}
        pip = subprocess.run([sys.executable, '-m', 'pip', 'install', '--disable-pip-version-check', '--no-index',

        print(result.stdout.strip())
        return 0

# GMRI | Dottie Hill v1.1 Runtime - 0.2.6 Offline Engineering Candidate

**Delivery mode:** ZIP archive for independent review. No remote diagnostics, host access, installation, or deployment are authorized by delivery of this archive. The installer scripts are dormant source files and must only be used after a separate explicit authorization by the operator. This release was prepared and tested in an isolated build container.

## v0.2.6 changes (offline, test-backed; not deployed)

- **Pi completion correlation is now mandatory.** Any completed Pi response missing
  `requestId` stays `UNCERTAIN` during both initial execution and GET-only
  restart reconciliation; mismatched IDs remain denied. The prior candidate
  accepted missing IDs, which could assign an unattributed answer to a mission.
  See `tests/test_pi_result_attribution.py` and `tests/test_durable_submission_recovery.py`.
- **Bounded release archive verification.** The read-only verifier now rejects
  excessive ZIP members, expanded size and compression ratio before decompressing
  the artifact. See `tests/test_archive_resource_bounds.py`.
- **Independent witness mechanism, not an independently signed release.**
  `scripts/verify_external_witness.py` verifies a detached Ed25519 review signature
  and binds it to the exact archive SHA-256, using a public-key fingerprint
  supplied **outside** the ZIP. See `docs/INDEPENDENT_WITNESS.md`.
- **Self-consistent packaging.** The release entrypoint identifies only v0.2.6,
  and version consistency is regression-tested. The build receipt, wheel and
  checksum manifest were recreated for this release.

**Still open:** no user-authorized Pi Durable host test, no actual model-provider
inference, no independent witness signature furnished, no OS-level tenancy and
zero production field gates accepted. This archive is not a field system.

## v0.2.5 changes (offline candidate)

Corrects the v0.2.4 README wheel reference and adds an npm v3 lockfile, exact
`@earendil-works/pi-codemode@1.3.0` / `quickjs-wasi@3.6.2` dependency tree,
actual registry SHA-512 metadata, a fail-closed supply-chain consistency gate,
and a CI real-QuickJS job on disposable Linux/macOS runners. See
`docs/RELEASE_0_2_5.md` and `PACKAGE_INTEGRITY_RECEIPT.json`. No GMRI host

### Adversarial release gate

`tests/test_security_adversarial.py` is an 11-case local abuse suite for bearer
permissions, identity scope, Code Mode tool grants, canonical state integrity,
source freshness and malicious ZIP entries. `docs/SECURITY_CHALLENGE.md` states
which properties these tests do **not** establish. A red-first test also caught
and closed a coordinated digest-rewrite weakness in the npm lock verifier.

## v0.2.4 changes (retained)

Built from the operator-supplied v0.2.3 source. **Execution mode is now explicit at mission creation** (`execution_mode: "provider" | "codemode"`), Code Mode cannot be claimed by the normal inference worker, incomplete read receipts cannot finish a Code Mode mission, and the Node sidecar no longer leaks private memories to stdout. The optional `scripts/verify_real_quickjs.py` gate uses the real pinned SDK and deliberately exits nonzero if it is unavailable. **The real QuickJS gate was blocked in this build environment, not passed.** See `docs/RELEASE_0_2_4.md` and `GLM_HANDOFF.md`.

## v0.2.3 changes (retained)

Pi Durable 202 acknowledgements are signed into mission state before polling, with explicit GET-only restart recovery. Pi completed answers must match request attribution and carry safe immutable entry IDs. Code Mode now has an operator-approved script-hash start, host-mediated read capabilities and receipt-backed agent-attributed finish, with a separate Node QuickJS sidecar source. **Real QuickJS/npm dependency execution was not possible** in this offline environment. Review `docs/RELEASE_0_2_4.md`, `docs/RELEASE_0_2_3.md` and `GLM_HANDOFF.md` for the verification boundary.

## What actually runs

- **GrizOS-owned local database and authority boundary.** Six persistent intelligence records (Dottie Hill + five separately attributed AEGIS members), not swappable model identities or disposable roleplay profiles.
- **Mission runtime.** Authenticated, idempotent read-only dispatch; fixed principal/delegatee authority; persistent mission records; evidence and receipts; interrupted external work held for reconciliation; operator-authorized independent AEGIS cross-check and model-generated Dottie synthesis.
- **Memory boundary.** Each intelligence has a distinct private namespace. AEGIS operational context and institutional context are separate; explicit private sharing/revocation is recorded; retrieved context does not automatically become first-hand memory. Direct writes to `institution:gmri` and `aegis:shared` are denied; population requires an owner-authenticated promotion grant followed by operator-approved promotion with receipts.
- **Provenance.** HMAC-chained event ledger and transaction-signed SHA-256 canonical state roots, source-attributed evidence, explicit evidence states, uncertainty, and model response attribution. Keys and operator credentials are never put in receipts.
- **Watch officer.** Materiality/consequence-based HOLD/BRIEF/INTERRUPT decisions, duplicate suppression, contradictory-source r

 from `$HOME/.local/share/gmri-dottie/secrets/operator.token` (permissions 0600). The web page never stores the token in localStorage. Do **not** expose HTTP directly to the internet. Remote iPad/Mac access requires an existing authenticated TLS/NetBird proxy with a separate ingress authorization design.

The daemon **does not require OMP/OpenRig to remain open**. It cannot access the lab's real providers until you bind them and set approved credentials. Only read-only model tools are supported; unrestricted Proxmox/device mutation is deliberately not implemented.

### Configure inference after checking live model/provider state

**Pi Durable:** the upstream `@earendil-works/pi-durable` package is a library exposing `Harness.open` and SQLite storage, **not** a turnkey HTTP service. The Dottie Python adapter targets a separate host-owned `/v1/sessions/...` gateway contract, which must be implemented, secured, and independently verified before binding. Do not assume installing Pi Durable alone exposes those routes. Use a distinct session per persistent intelligence; ensure the assigned agent reports `config.readOnly: true` on `GET /v1/sessions/:session/agents/main`. Put the device's `DPI_TOKEN` in the local `secrets/pi.token` file (owner-only permission 0600), or inject `DOTTIE_PI_TOKEN` through the host's private secret management. The operator console can then bind that dedicated Pi session to Dottie. Example CLI equivalent:

```sh
dottie-hill bind-model --data "$HOME/.local/share/gmri-dottie" \
  --member dottie-hill --provider pi-durable \
  --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8900 --session dottie-hill \
  --reason 'private Pi session verified readOnly and reachable'
```

Change `base-url` only to your *actually verified* Pi endpoint. Do not assume `8900` is your installation's port. A saved binding is not a live inference acceptance receipt.

**Ollama:** bind only after confirming the *exact* tag in the correct installed local/cloud provider. The October 2026 historical `:cloud` and `ollama` versus `ollama-cloud` confusion is not evidence the model itself is down. # GMRI Dottie Hill v0.2.6 — evidence-based repair, not field acceptance

## Baseline and scope

Built in an isolated ChatGPT Linux container using the exact user-supplied
v0.2.5 archive; source ZIP SHA-256:
`ebd2dd62cdf9752e70f2c0a3b8246e7edeb45c31d939aa98b0ead5a06f0b4b4c`.
No GMRI host or operator account was accessed. No deployment was performed.

## Red-first defects and fixes

1. **Missing Pi request attribution** — a `done` answer with valid `entryId`
   but absent `requestId` was promoted to `DONE` or `RECONCILED_EXTERNAL`.
   Tests failed for synchronous, async and GET-only restart paths.
   `ModelRouter._pi_attributed_answer` now requires a matching mission ID in
   all completed response types. Fixtures for valid provider behavior echo
   the submitted `requestId`. The local signed ledger remains consistent and
   unknown external outcomes remain uncertain, with no automatic POST replay.
2. **Archive verifier resource exhaustion** — checksum-valid but adversarial
   compression ratio and huge ZIP member counts both passed verification.
   `verify_release.py` now rejects archives before decompression when any
   expanded file exceeds 32 MiB, sum exceeds 256 MiB, member count exceeds
   2048, or compression ratio exceeds 256:1. This is a reviewer DoS bound,
   not a security claim about arbitrary ZIP parsers elsewhere in the stack.
3. **No enforceable independent signature check** — existing `SHA256SUMS`
   is self-consistent but unauthenticated. New optional Ed25519 verifier
   requires out-of-band public-key fingerprint; negative tests deny archive
   mutation, statement mutation, key substitution and absent signatures.
   **No independent signature has been issued for this candidate.**
4. **Stale release front matter** — the v0.2.5 `START_HERE.md` included a
   second v0.2.4 primary heading and pointed at the wrong wheel. New test
   requires one current heading and matching wheel.

cat > "$W/integration/pi-durable-owner/verify_real_sdk.mjs" <<'EOF'
/** Genuine Pi Durable SQLite reopen gate; NEVER fakes a green pass. */
import {mkdtemp,rm} from 'node:fs/promises';
import {tmpdir} from 'node:os';
import {join} from 'node:path';
import {createRequire} from 'node:module';
const require=createRequire(import.meta.url);
function fail(why){process.stderr.write(`BLOCKED: ${why}\n`);process.exitCode=2;}
async function main(){
  const [major,minor]=process.versions.node.split('.').map(Number);
  if(major<22||(major===22&&minor<19))return fail('Node 22.19.0+ is required');
  for(const pkg of ['@earendil-works/pi-durable','@earendil-works/pi-ai','@earendil-works/chord']){
    let meta;try{meta=require(`${pkg}/package.json`)}catch{return fail(`required reviewed package unavailable: ${pkg}`)}
    if(meta.version!=='1.3.0')return fail(`SDK version mismatch for ${pkg}`);
  }
  const [{Harness,createRegistry},{openNodeSqliteStorage},{createModels},{BACKGROUND_CONTEXT}]=await Promise.all([
    import('@earendil-works/pi-durable'),
    import('@earendil-works/pi-durable/storage/sqlite/node'),
    import('@earendil-works/pi-ai/models'),
    import('@earendil-works/chord/context'),
  ]);
  const dir=await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(),'gmri-durable-sdk-'));
  try{
    const file=join(dir,'state.sqlite');const models=createModels();const registry=createRegistry();
    const h1=await Harness.open(await openNodeSqliteStorage(file),{models,registry},BACKGROUND_CONTEXT);
    const root1=await h1.root(BACKGROUND_CONTEXT,{agent:{tools:[],modelTools:[],extensions:[]}});
    const id=root1.id;
    const agent1=await root1.agent(BACKGROUND_CONTEXT);
    if(agent1.tools.length||agent1.callable.length)throw new Error('Unexpected provider tools');
    await h1.close(BACKGROUND_CONTEXT);
    const h2=await Harness.open(await openNodeSqliteStorage(file),{models,registry},BACKGROUND_CONTEXT);
    try{
      const root2=await h2.root(BACKGROUND_CONTEXT);
      if(root2.id!==id)throw new Error('Conversation identity changed across SQLite reopen');
      const a=await root2.agent(BACKGROUND_CONTEXT);
      if(a.tools.length||a.callable.length)throw new Error('Tools appeared after reopen');
    }finally{await h2.close(BACKGROUND_CONTEXT)}
    process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify({gate:'PI_DURABLE_REAL_SDK_SQLITE_REOPEN',status:'PASS',version:'1.3.0',
      real_inference:false,os_tenancy:false,production_accepted:false})+'\n');
  }finally{await rm(dir,{recursive:true,force:true})}
}
main().catch(()=>fail('real SDK SQLite smoke did not pass; no completion receipt issued'));
EOF

## Concrete repaired defects, with falsifiers

1. **Primary-evidence label injection:** The v0.2.6 API allowed an operator
   to self-label source material `VERIFIED_PRIMARY` using any nonempty receipt.
   Now a separately provisioned Ed25519 public key and out-of-band fingerprint

   exact content hash, reviewer, review timestamp, and receipt. A signed
   *assertion* is still not proof that the asserted source is true. Legacy
   self-labelled rows are quarantined **on read**, without deleting history.
   `tests/test_primary_evidence_witness.py`, `test_primary_evidence_legacy.py`.

   The HTTP gate independently authenticates a bearer, rejects all Pi-offered

   The transcript commit and finalization marker share a Pi transaction.

# Dottie Hill v0.2.7 — bounded Pi Durable host candidate and witnessed evidence

**Status:** OFFLINE ENGINEERING CANDIDATE. Not field accepted; no GMRI machine,
account, cloud host or production service was accessed. This is a deployable
*source interface* and Python wheel, not a proven end-to-end intelligence.

## Concrete repaired defects, with falsifiers

1. **Primary-evidence label injection:** The v0.2.6 API allowed an operator
   to self-label source material `VERIFIED_PRIMARY` using any nonempty receipt.
   Now a separately provisioned Ed25519 public key and out-of-band fingerprint
   must authenticate a canonical signed statement binding source ref, class,
   exact content hash, reviewer, review timestamp, and receipt. A signed
   *assertion* is still not proof that the asserted source is true. Legacy
   self-labelled rows are quarantined **on read**, without deleting history.
   `tests/test_primary_evidence_witness.py`, `test_primary_evidence_legacy.py`.
2. **Pi runtime owner absent:** Implemented optional source for a one-identity
   Pi Durable 1.3.0 SQLite-backed host under `integration/pi-durable-owner/`.
   The HTTP gate independently authenticates a bearer, rejects all Pi-offered
   tools, pins the session, persists the requestId/submissionId acceptance map
   with fsync **before** returning 202, and uses GET-only reconciliation.
   The actual `Harness.open`, `root.submit`, `harness.submission.wait` and
   `root.commit(AssistantEntry)` calls follow the reviewed upstream v1.3.0 API.
   The transcript commit and finalization marker share a Pi transaction.
3. **Pi submission attribution conflated with entry attribution:** Python
   now accepts a distinct `submissionRef` only after matching the originally
   recorded 202 acknowledgement; mismatched or mixed entry/submission refs
   remain `UNCERTAIN`. During the first cross-language test the handler
   incorrectly lost the acknowledged ID after GET changed HTTP 202 to 200;
   that test was RED before the repair and GREEN afterward.
4. **Production-staging distinction:** Python↔Node real HTTP tests are run
   with an openly identified FAKE upstream SDK, **not fake-proclaimed live
   inference**. `node integration/pi-durable-owner/verify_real_sdk.mjs` is an
   independent real-SDK SQLite reopen gate that fails nonzero when Node or
   exact reviewed packages are unavailable. It has not passed on the builder.

# GMRI | Dottie Hill v1.1 Runtime - 0.2.7 Offline Engineering Candidate

**Delivery mode:** ZIP archive for independent review. No remote diagnostics, host access, installation, or deployment are authorized by delivery of this archive. The installer scripts are dormant source files and must only be used after a separate explicit authorization by the operator. This release was prepared and tested in an isolated build container.

**Repository artifact:** an executable, versioned Dottie/AEGIS operational component built from the original GMRI GrizOS PRD v1.1 and the 7 October 2026 production constitution. It is **not** the finished GrizOS operating system or a remotely accepted Dottie deployment.

## v0.2.7 changes — bounded Pi host source, verified primary-review claims

- A detached Ed25519 primary-source review statement is now required to
  label evidence VERIFIED_PRIMARY; the signing key fingerprint comes from an
  independent channel, and legacy string-only labels are downgraded on read.
- Added an optional one-identity Pi Durable v1.3.0 owner HTTP bridge with
  fsynced request/submission correlation, real SDK loader, empty provider tools,
  strict actor/session routing and transaction-bound answer finalization.
- Python now correctly retains a 202 submission handle across GET polling
  and distinguishes a submission reference from an immutable entry ID.
- Real HTTP Python↔Node integration is tested using an explicitly fake SDK,
  not misrepresented as real inference; upstream real-SDK dependency installation,
  SQL task resume, real inference and field testing remain OPEN.
- See `docs/RELEASE_0_2_7.md` and `integration/pi-durable-owner/README.md`.

## v0.2.6 changes (offline, test-backed; not deployed)

- **Pi completion correlation is now mandatory.** Any completed Pi response missing
  `requestId` stays `UNCERTAIN` during both initial execution and GET-only
  restart reconciliation; mismatched IDs remain denied. The prior candidate
  accepted missing IDs, which could assign an unattributed answer to a mission.
  See `tests/test_pi_result_attribution.py` and `tests/test_durable_submission_recovery.py`.
- **Bounded release archive verification.** The read-only verifier now rejects
  excessive ZIP members, expanded size and compression ratio before decompressing
  the artifact. See `tests/test_archive_resource_bounds.py`.
- **Independent witness mechanism, not an independently signed release.**
  `scripts/verify_external_witness.py` verifies a detached Ed25519 review signature
  and binds it to the exact archive SHA-256, using a public-key fingerprint
  supplied **outside** the ZIP. See `docs/INDEPENDENT_WITNESS.md`.
- **Self-consistent packaging.** The release entrypoint identifies only v0.2.6,
  and version consistency is regression-tested. The build receipt, wheel and
  checksum manifest were recreated for this release.

inference, no independent witness signature furnished, no OS-level tenancy and
zero production field gates accepted. This archive is not a field system.

def tree_sha256():
    digest=hashlib.sha256(b'gmri.dottie.release.tree.v1\0')
    for path in sorted(ROOT.rglob('*')):
        relative=path.relative_to(ROOT)
        if any(part in SKIP for part in relative.parts) or path.is_dir():continue
        if path.name in ('LOCAL_TEST_RECEIPT.json','RELEASE_BUILD_RECEIPT.json','SHA256SUMS.txt') or path.suffix in ('.pyc','.pyo'):continue
        digest.update(str(relative).encode()+b'\0')
        digest.update(hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).digest())
    return digest.hexdigest()

/**
 * Opt-in, one-identity Pi Durable host. NEVER auto-launched by the release.
 * Uses the real @earendil-works/pi-durable Harness.open(SQLite), not a fake SDK.
 * The host exposes ONLY Dottie's authenticated submit/status contract.
 * Existence/compilation of this file is not a live model inference receipt.
 *
 * Based on upstream Pi v1.3.0 packages/durable/README.md quick start.

import {lstat, readFile, mkdir} from 'node:fs/promises';
import {resolve, join} from 'node:path';
import process from 'node:process';
import {createOwnerServer, assistantText} from './pi_owner_contract.mjs';
import {createHash} from 'node:crypto';

async function runtime(){
  const [major,minor]=process.versions.node.split('.').map(Number);
  if(major<22 || (major===22&&minor<19))throw new Error('PINNED_NODE_VERSION_REQUIRED');
  const identity=process.env.DOTTIE_PI_OWNER_ID;
  if(!/^(?:dottie-hill|aegis-(?:dugan|jones|morita|falsworth|dernier))$/.test(identity||''))
    throw new Error('EXPLICIT_SINGLE_IDENTITY_REQUIRED');
  const modelId=process.env.DOTTIE_PI_MODEL_ID;
  if(typeof modelId!=='string'||!modelId.trim()||modelId.length>180)
    throw new Error('EXPLICIT_PROVIDER_MODEL_REQUIRED');
  if(!process.env.OPENAI_API_KEY)throw new Error('LIVE_PROVIDER_CREDENTIAL_NOT_PROVISIONED');
  const tokenFile=process.env.DOTTIE_PI_OWNER_TOKEN_FILE;
  const data=process.env.DOTTIE_PI_OWNER_DATA;
  if(!tokenFile||!data)throw new Error('EXTERNAL_TOKEN_AND_PRIVATE_DATA_DIRECTORY_REQUIRED');
  const keyStat=await lstat(tokenFile);
  if(!keyStat.isFile()||keyStat.isSymbolicLink()||(keyStat.mode & 0o077)!==0||
      (process.getuid && keyStat.uid!==process.getuid()))
    throw new Error('OWNER_TOKEN_FILE_MUST_BE_PRIVATE_AND_OWNED');
  const token=(await readFile(tokenFile,'utf8')).trim();
  if(token.length<32||token.length>256)throw new Error('OWNER_TOKEN_TOO_WEAK');
  const dir=resolve(data);
  await mkdir(dir,{recursive:true,mode:0o700});
  const stat=await lstat(dir);
  if(!stat.isDirectory()||stat.isSymbolicLink()||(stat.mode&0o077)!==0||
     (process.getuid && stat.uid!==process.getuid()))
    throw new Error('OWNER_DATA_DIRECTORY_MUST_BE_PRIVATE_AND_OWNED');
  // Real upstream imports fail closed when the reviewed/pinned dependency
  // closure is missing. This release does NOT install dependencies for you.
  const [{BACKGROUND_CONTEXT}, {createModels}, {openaiProvider},
    {Harness,createRegistry,defineDoc,AssistantEntry}, {openNodeSqliteStorage}] = await Promise.all([
      import('@earendil-works/chord/context'),
      import('@earendil-works/pi-ai/models'),
      import('@earendil-works/pi-ai/providers/openai'),
      import('@earendil-works/pi-durable'),
      import('@earendil-works/pi-durable/storage/sqlite/node'),
    ]);
  const context=BACKGROUND_CONTEXT;
  const models=createModels();
  models.setProvider(openaiProvider());
  const registry=createRegistry();  // NO upstream tool extensions installed.
  const harness=await Harness.open(await openNodeSqliteStorage(join(dir,'pi.sqlite')),
    {models,registry,settings:{retry:{maxRetries:0}}},context);
  try{
    const root=await harness.root(context, {agent:{
      model:{provider:'openai',modelId},tools:[],modelTools:[],extensions:[]}});
    const agent=await root.agent(context);
    if(agent.model?.provider!=='openai'||agent.model?.modelId!==modelId)
      throw new Error('STORED_MODEL_BINDING_DIFFERS_FROM_OPERATOR_CHOICE');
    if(!Array.isArray(agent.tools)||agent.tools.length||
       !Array.isArray(agent.callable)||agent.callable.length)
      throw new Error('UPSTREAM_TOOL_ISOLATION_NOT_PROVEN');
    // The assistant transcript and the at-most-once finalization marker are
    // committed in the SAME upstream Pi Durable transaction. No external
    // marker is authoritative for an assistant message. Repeated GETs and
    // restarts obtain the same sealed answer without a second tx.entry.
    const Finalizations=defineDoc({kind:'gmri.dottie.pi-owner-finalizations',version:1,
      scope:'conversation',history:'latest',fork:'initial',initial:()=>({rows:{}})});
    const finalize=async ({submissionId,settled})=>{
      if(settled.status!=='done'||settled.type!=='input')
        throw new Error('PI_SUBMISSION_NOT_ANSWERED');
      const hash=createHash('sha256').update(JSON.stringify(settled.answer)).digest('hex');
      return root.commit(async tx=>{
        const doc=await tx.doc(Finalizations,root.id);
        const previous=doc.rows[submissionId];
        if(previous){
          if(previous.sha256!==hash||typeof previous.text!=='string')
            throw new Error('PI_FINALIZATION_CONTENT_CONFLICT');
          return {text:previous.text};
        }
        const entry=await tx.entry(AssistantEntry,settled.answer);
        const text=assistantText(entry?.model?.[0]);
        doc.rows[submissionId]={sha256:hash,text};
        return {text};
      },context);
    };
    harness.resume();
    const owner=await createOwnerServer({root,harness,context,token,session:identity,dataDirectory:dir,finalize});
    const port=Number(process.env.DOTTIE_PI_OWNER_PORT||8769);
    if(!Number.isInteger(port)||port<1024||port>65535)throw new Error('INVALID_LOOPBACK_PORT');
    await owner.listen(port);
    // Status is not an inference or acceptance receipt; no secrets or model text.
    process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify({state:'LOCAL_PI_OWNER_LISTENING',identity,
      substrate:'pi-durable-sqlite',bind:'127.0.0.1',port,
      production_accepted:false})+'\n');
    const shutdown=async()=>{
      await owner.close(); await harness.close(context);process.exit(0);
    };
    process.once('SIGTERM',()=>void shutdown());
    process.once('SIGINT',()=>void shutdown());
  }catch(e){await harness.close(context);throw e}
}
runtime().catch(e=>{
  // Never print provider response bodies, API tokens or model-visible context.
  const message=String(e?.message||'').startsWith('ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND')
    ? 'PINNED_PI_SDK_DEPENDENCIES_UNAVAILABLE':'RUNTIME_PRECONDITION_OR_SDK_FAILURE';
  process.stderr.write(`Pi owner refused startup: ${message}\n`);
  process.exitCode=2;
});

# Dottie Hill v0.2.7 — bounded Pi Durable host candidate and witnessed evidence

**Status:** OFFLINE ENGINEERING CANDIDATE. Not field accepted; no GMRI machine,
account, cloud host or production service was accessed. This is a deployable
*source interface* and Python wheel, not a proven end-to-end intelligence.

## Concrete repaired defects, with falsifiers

1. **Primary-evidence label injection:** The v0.2.6 API allowed an operator
   to self-label source material `VERIFIED_PRIMARY` using any nonempty receipt.
   Now a separately provisioned Ed25519 public key and out-of-band fingerprint
   must authenticate a canonical signed statement binding source ref, class,
   exact content hash, reviewer, review timestamp, and receipt. A signed
   *assertion* is still not proof that the asserted source is true. Legacy
   self-labelled rows are quarantined **on read**, without deleting history.
   `tests/test_primary_evidence_witness.py`, `test_primary_evidence_legacy.py`.
2. **Pi runtime owner absent:** Implemented optional source for a one-identity
   Pi Durable 1.3.0 SQLite-backed host under `integration/pi-durable-owner/`.
   The HTTP gate independently authenticates a bearer, rejects all Pi-offered
   tools, pins the session, persists the requestId/submissionId acceptance map
   with fsync **before** returning 202, and uses GET-only reconciliation.
   The actual `Harness.open`, `root.submit`, `harness.submission.wait` and
   `root.commit(AssistantEntry)` calls follow the reviewed upstream v1.3.0 API.
   The transcript commit and finalization marker share a Pi transaction.
3. **Pi submission attribution conflated with entry attribution:** Python
   now accepts a distinct `submissionRef` only after matching the originally
   recorded 202 acknowledgement; mismatched or mixed entry/submission refs
   remain `UNCERTAIN`. During the first cross-language test the handler
   incorrectly lost the acknowledged ID after GET changed HTTP 202 to 200;
   that test was RED before the repair and GREEN afterward.
4. **Production-staging distinction:** Python↔Node real HTTP tests are run
   with an openly identified FAKE upstream SDK, **not fake-proclaimed live
   inference**. `node integration/pi-durable-owner/verify_real_sdk.mjs` is an
   independent real-SDK SQLite reopen gate that fails nonzero when Node or
   exact reviewed packages are unavailable. It has not passed on the builder.

## Not closed: external authority and production

- No exact externally audited npm *install closure* for the new Pi owner
  runtime. Its three direct 1.3.0 pins are documented, but until a complete
  immutable lock and authenticated tarballs exist the optional host cannot
  be installed or field-accepted by this ZIP. The separately pinned QuickJS
  lock is unaffected.
- No real Pi SDK code was run on this isolated builder; Node was 22.16.0,
  below pinned 22.19.0, and new packages could not be downloaded.
- No live inference through an actual model/provider or with credentials.
- No per-intelligence OS principal/tenancy independently attested. Separate
  protocol sessions and source folder modes do **not** establish this.
- No independent witness signed **this release**; verifier machinery is
  present but no out-of-band signature was received.
- No observed hosted CI execution or installed native GMRI services.
- **Zero of the original eighteen field acceptance gates were completed.**

## Core ontological constraints preserved

GrizOS is the environment and authority router, not an intelligence. Dottie
Hill v1.1 is the principal persistent intelligence. The five AEGIS identities
are independent peers with per-agent memories, not Dottie's components. Pi
Durable and Pi Code Mode remain replaceable execution substrates. GEV is a
world-state projection rather than autobiographical memory. Source evidence,
interpretations, signed attestations and agent outputs remain distinct.

Review `GLM_HANDOFF.md`, `RED_PRIMARY_WITNESS_REPRO.txt`,
`RED_PI_OWNER_ATTRIBUTION_REPRO.txt`, `RED_PI_OWNER_COMMIT_REPRO.txt`,
`RED_PI_OWNER_CROSS_LANGUAGE_REPRO.txt` and verified `LOCAL_TEST_RECEIPT.json`.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Reproducible local release checks, NOT GMRI production acceptance."""
from __future__ import annotations
import datetime
import os
import argparse
import hashlib
import json
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
import sys

ROOT=Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
COMMANDS=[
    ['python3','-m','pytest','-q','-p','no:cacheprovider','tests'],
    ['node','--check','src/dottie_hill/static/console.js'],
    ['node','--check','integration/codemode/codemode_host.mjs'],
    ['node','--check','integration/pi-durable-owner/pi_owner_runtime.mjs'],
    ['node','--test','integration/pi-durable-owner/pi_owner_contract.test.mjs'],
    ['python3','scripts/verify_supply_chain.py'],
    ['python3','scripts/check_syntax.py'],
    ['python3','scripts/install_local.py','--dry-run','--target','mac'],
]
SKIP={'.git','.pytest_cache','__pycache__','.venv','build','dist','gmri_dottie_hill.egg-info'}

def tree_sha256():
    digest=hashlib.sha256(b'gmri.dottie.release.tree.v1\0')
    for path in sorted(ROOT.rglob('*')):
        relative=path.relative_to(ROOT)
        if any(part in SKIP for part in relative.parts) or path.is_dir():continue
        if path.name in ('LOCAL_TEST_RECEIPT.json','RELEASE_BUILD_RECEIPT.json','SHA256SUMS.txt') or path.suffix in ('.pyc','.pyo'):continue
        digest.update(str(relative).encode()+b'\0')
        digest.update(hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).digest())
    return digest.hexdigest()

def main(argv=None):
    parser=argparse.ArgumentParser(description='Read-only local source checks (not production acceptance)')
    parser.add_argument('--receipt-path',type=Path,help='Optional NEW receipt path OUTSIDE the release archive; never overwrites existing evidence')
    args=parser.parse_args(argv)
    receipt_path=args.receipt_path.expanduser().resolve() if args.receipt_path is not None else None
    if receipt_path is not None and receipt_path.is_relative_to(ROOT.resolve()):
        raise ValueError('refusing to write a release check receipt inside the release tree')
    checks=[]
    child_env = {**os.environ, 'PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE': '1'}
    for cmd in COMMANDS:
        p=subprocess.run([sys.executable if arg=='python3' else arg for arg in cmd],cwd=ROOT,env=child_env,stdout=subprocess.PIPE,stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,text=True,timeout=240)
        checks.append({'command':' '.join(cmd),'exit_code':p.returncode,'last_output_lines':p.stdout.splitlines()[-10:]})
    good=all(x['exit_code']==0 for x in checks)
    receipt={'schema':'gmri.dottie.local-release.v2',
      'built_at_utc':datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).isoformat(),
      'state':'LOCAL_TEST_PASS' if good else 'LOCAL_TEST_FAIL',
      'checks':checks,'source_tree_sha256':tree_sha256(),
      'prod_acceptance':'LIVE_ACCEPTANCE_NOT_PASSED',
      'actual_gmri_host_access':False,'real_model_inference_verified':False,
      'gev_ct112_deployed':False,'apple_offline_field_verified':False,
      'chromium_browser_navigation':'NOT_RUN_THIS_BUILD',
      'interpretation':'Local test outcome is not a live GMRI product acceptance or Mac deployment receipt.'}
    formatted=json.dumps(receipt,indent=2,sort_keys=True)+'\n'
    if receipt_path is not None:
        # Exclusive creation protects previous receipts; never mutate published files.
        with receipt_path.open('x',encoding='utf-8') as output:
            output.write(formatted)
    print(formatted,end='')
    return 0 if good else 2

if __name__=='__main__':raise SystemExit(main())

async function runtime(){
  const [major,minor]=process.versions.node.split('.').map(Number);
  if(major<22 || (major===22&&minor<19))throw new Error('PINNED_NODE_VERSION_REQUIRED');
  const identity=process.env.DOTTIE_PI_OWNER_ID;
  if(!/^(?:dottie-hill|aegis-(?:dugan|jones|morita|falsworth|dernier))$/.test(identity||''))
    throw new Error('EXPLICIT_SINGLE_IDENTITY_REQUIRED');
  const modelId=process.env.DOTTIE_PI_MODEL_ID;
  if(typeof modelId!=='string'||!modelId.trim()||modelId.length>180)
    throw new Error('EXPLICIT_PROVIDER_MODEL_REQUIRED');
  if(!process.env.OPENAI_API_KEY)throw new Error('LIVE_PROVIDER_CREDENTIAL_NOT_PROVISIONED');
  const tokenFile=process.env.DOTTIE_PI_OWNER_TOKEN_FILE;
  const data=process.env.DOTTIE_PI_OWNER_DATA;
  if(!tokenFile||!data)throw new Error('EXTERNAL_TOKEN_AND_PRIVATE_DATA_DIRECTORY_REQUIRED');
  const keyStat=await lstat(tokenFile);
  if(!keyStat.isFile()||keyStat.isSymbolicLink()||(keyStat.mode & 0o077)!==0||
      (process.getuid && keyStat.uid!==process.getuid()))
    throw new Error('OWNER_TOKEN_FILE_MUST_BE_PRIVATE_AND_OWNED');
  const token=(await readFile(tokenFile,'utf8')).trim();
  if(token.length<32||token.length>256)throw new Error('OWNER_TOKEN_TOO_WEAK');
  const dir=resolve(data);
  await mkdir(dir,{recursive:true,mode:0o700});
  const stat=await lstat(dir);
  if(!stat.isDirectory()||stat.isSymbolicLink()||(stat.mode&0o077)!==0||
     (process.getuid && stat.uid!==process.getuid()))
    throw new Error('OWNER_DATA_DIRECTORY_MUST_BE_PRIVATE_AND_OWNED');
  // Real upstream imports fail closed when the reviewed/pinned dependency
  // closure is missing. This release does NOT install dependencies for you.
  const [{BACKGROUND_CONTEXT}, {createModels}, {openaiProvider},
    {Harness,createRegistry,defineDoc,AssistantEntry}, {openNodeSqliteStorage}] = await Promise.all([
      import('@earendil-works/chord/context'),
      import('@earendil-works/pi-ai/models'),
      import('@earendil-works/pi-ai/providers/openai'),
      import('@earendil-works/pi-durable'),
      import('@earendil-works/pi-durable/storage/sqlite/node'),
    ]);
  const context=BACKGROUND_CONTEXT;
  const models=createModels();
  models.setProvider(openaiProvider());
  const registry=createRegistry();  // NO upstream tool extensions installed.
  const harness=await Harness.open(await openNodeSqliteStorage(join(dir,'pi.sqlite')),
    {models,registry,settings:{retry:{maxRetries:0}}},context);
  try{
    const root=await harness.root(context, {agent:{
      model:{provider:'openai',modelId},tools:[],modelTools:[],extensions:[]}});
    const agent=await root.agent(context);
    if(agent.model?.provider!=='openai'||agent.model?.modelId!==modelId)
      throw new Error('STORED_MODEL_BINDING_DIFFERS_FROM_OPERATOR_CHOICE');
    if(!Array.isArray(agent.tools)||agent.tools.length||
       !Array.isArray(agent.callable)||agent.callable.length)
      throw new Error('UPSTREAM_TOOL_ISOLATION_NOT_PROVEN');
    // The assistant transcript and the at-most-once finalization marker are
    // committed in the SAME upstream Pi Durable transaction. No external
    // marker is authoritative for an assistant message. Repeated GETs and
    // restarts obtain the same sealed answer without a second tx.entry.
    const Finalizations=defineDoc({kind:'gmri.dottie.pi-owner-finalizations',version:1,
      scope:'conversation',history:'latest',fork:'initial',initial:()=>({rows:{}})});
    const finalize=async ({submissionId,settled})=>{
      if(settled.status!=='done'||settled.type!=='input')
        throw new Error('PI_SUBMISSION_NOT_ANSWERED');
      const hash=createHash('sha256').update(JSON.stringify(settled.answer)).digest('hex');
      return root.commit(async tx=>{
        const doc=await tx.doc(Finalizations,root.id);
        const previous=doc.rows[submissionId];
        if(previous){
          if(previous.sha256!==hash||typeof previous.text!=='string')
            throw new Error('PI_FINALIZATION_CONTENT_CONFLICT');
          return {text:previous.text};
        }
        const entry=await tx.entry(AssistantEntry,settled.answer);
        const text=assistantText(entry?.model?.[0]);
        doc.rows[submissionId]={sha256:hash,text};
        return {text};
      },context);
    };
    harness.resume();
    const owner=await createOwnerServer({root,harness,context,token,session:identity,dataDirectory:dir,finalize});
    const port=Number(process.env.DOTTIE_PI_OWNER_PORT||8769);
    if(!Number.isInteger(port)||port<1024||port>65535)throw new Error('INVALID_LOOPBACK_PORT');
    await owner.listen(port);
    // Status is not an inference or acceptance receipt; no secrets or model text.
    process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify({state:'LOCAL_PI_OWNER_LISTENING',identity,
      substrate:'pi-durable-sqlite',bind:'127.0.0.1',port,
      production_accepted:false})+'\n');
    const shutdown=async()=>{
      await owner.close(); await harness.close(context);process.exit(0);
    };
    process.once('SIGTERM',()=>void shutdown());
    process.once('SIGINT',()=>void shutdown());
  }catch(e){await harness.close(context);throw e}
}
runtime().catch(e=>{
  // Never print provider response bodies, API tokens or model-visible context.
  const message=String(e?.message||'').startsWith('ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND')
    ? 'PINNED_PI_SDK_DEPENDENCIES_UNAVAILABLE':'RUNTIME_PRECONDITION_OR_SDK_FAILURE';
  process.stderr.write(`Pi owner refused startup: ${message}\n`);
  process.exitCode=2;

# Pi Durable 1.3.0 host bridge — real SDK boundary, pending live acceptance

**Function:** One distinct Pi owner **per intelligence** (one OS principal, one
private SQLite store, one gateway token). The code is not deployed by this ZIP.
Dottie, not Pi, still owns identity, authority, memory scopes and evidence.

Code: `pi_owner_runtime.mjs` loads the *real* upstream
`@earendil-works/pi-durable` v1.3.0 `Harness.open`, SQLite storage and one
`openaiProvider` model; `pi_owner_contract.mjs` is the HTTP adapter. The
published `@earendil-works/pi-durable` upstream quickstart is the normative
source: https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v1.3.0/packages/durable/README.md

## Required operator-controlled runtime inputs

- Node >=22.19.0, exact audited versions of `@earendil-works/pi-durable`,
  `@earendil-works/pi-ai`, and `@earendil-works/chord` **all at 1.3.0** and
  their transitive dependency closure installed under a separately reviewed
  immutable lock. This ZIP cannot build that new lock: registry access was
  unavailable in the isolated builder. No inference passes on this builder.
- `DOTTIE_PI_OWNER_ID` one of the six registered identities;
  `DOTTIE_PI_MODEL_ID` an explicitly authorized model available from the real
  OpenAI provider, no model is guessed;
  `DOTTIE_PI_OWNER_DATA` private per-principal directory (0700),
  `DOTTIE_PI_OWNER_TOKEN_FILE` external token (0600, 32+ characters),
  `OPENAI_API_KEY` supplied through approved secret management;
  `DOTTIE_PI_OWNER_PORT` loopback listening port (default 8769).
- A separate Dottie `pi-durable` binding matching the identity as session,
  agent `main`, to `http://127.0.0.1:<port>`; Dottie `DOTTIE_PI_TOKEN` must match
  the separately provisioned host token. All tool exposure is **denied**.

## Exact test contract / limits

`node --test integration/pi-durable-owner/pi_owner_contract.test.mjs` tests
actual Node HTTP, bearer authentication, per-session scoping, SDK-shaped
submission, fsynced dual-index attribution, hash collision rejection, finite
wait budget and tool-denial checks, with a conspicuously **fake** SDK in the
unit test only. `python -m pytest tests/test_pi_durable_owner_attribution.py`
checks Python's boundary accepts *submission* reference only when tied to
acknowledged upstream acceptance. Neither test calls a model or proves the real
SDK loaded. An SDK bootstrap uses `Harness.open(...openNodeSqliteStorage())`,
`root.submit(...requestId)` and `harness.submission(id).wait()` as described
in upstream docs; it fails on missing dependency or credentials.

### Critical known limits

1. Source compiles locally and contract tests pass; **real SDK install,
   execution, restart, inference, and hosted CI NOT verified** on this builder.
2. SQLite defaults to WAL `synchronous=NORMAL` upstream, which has process-crash
   but not newest-write power-failure guarantees. The Dottie HTTP gateway also
   retains its separate acknowledgement map; full atomic cross-store commit
   is not established. An orphaned accepted POST remains uncertain, never an
   excuse to re-dispatch a possibly executed mission automatically.
3. This process is one-identity at the protocol level, **not independently
   attested OS isolation**. Launching six Node processes as the same Unix user
   does not meet the original tenancy gate.
4. Only the specified OpenAI provider is wired in the optional owner. Model
   availability, request output, provider cost, inference and real identities
   must be established at the authorized field or staging environment.
5. The signed primary-evidence witness path in Python is distinct; successful
   inference is only attributed, not source-truth certification.

To perform real acceptance the operator/reviewer must first supply a locked,
reviewed npm tree outside this ZIP, provision a dedicated principal per owner,
and run the genuine SDK/inference test in that environment. Do not install,
run, or restart services on GMRI hosts from this archive without approval.
